title: Cost-of-Living Protests Draw 106,000 Across France as BFMTV Crew Is Attacked in Lyon
dek: The Interior Ministry put turnout at 106,000 on the fifth weekend of demonstrations, with 219 arrests and violent incidents in several cities, including an assault on a television crew in Lyon.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Demonstrators marching in a protest in Paris on October 17, 2026; the image predates the November 14 demonstrations

keyPoints: The French Interior Ministry said about 106,000 people joined protests across France on Saturday, including 24,000 in Paris, France 24 reported. It described the turnout as the lowest in recent weeks.
Estimates differ: a related franceinfo headline gave a range of 106,000 (Interior Ministry) to 200,000 (a youth union coalition).

Protesters attacked a BFMTV crew of two journalists and two security guards in Lyon, the Rhône prefecture said. The prefect condemned the attacks, and the Interior Ministry said one suspected attacker had been arrested.
About 70,000 police officers and gendarmes were deployed across 50 to 60 planned marches, France 24 reported, citing the ministry.
body:
About 106,000 people joined protests across France on Saturday over the cost of living, inequality and government policy, the French Interior Ministry said, in the fifth weekend of demonstrations this autumn. [France 24 reported](https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261114-live-france-mobilises-in-fifth-wave-of-student-protests) that the ministry put the Paris figure at 24,000 and described the turnout as the lowest in recent weeks.

## Turnout and policing

The Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students organised the day of action, according to France 24. Around 70,000 police officers and gendarmes were deployed across 50 to 60 planned marches. The ministry said the situation was generally under control despite clashes in several cities, including Marseille, Grenoble, Lyon, Bordeaux, Montpellier, Toulouse and Lille, where projectiles and mortars were thrown at officers. Ten officers sustained minor injuries, and the ministry had recorded 219 arrests by 6 p.m. local time.

[Franceinfo reported](https://franceinfo.fr/societe/manifestations/manifestations-du-14-novembre-une-equipe-de-bfmtv-agressee-en-marge-de-la-mobilisation-a-lyon_8282714.html) that national estimates ranged from 106,000 by the Interior Ministry to 200,000 by a youth union coalition. Meridian has not verified the higher figure.

## The attack on the BFMTV crew

Franceinfo reported that a BFMTV crew of two journalists and two security guards was attacked by protesters on the margins of the Lyon procession in the afternoon. Citing the Rhône prefecture, it said protesters threw themselves on the crew in what the prefecture described as a very violent assault, prompting riot police to charge to protect them. Franceinfo said the prefect condemned the attacks “in the strongest terms” and reminded the public that press freedom is fundamental to democracy.

An independent freelance witness told AFP, as franceinfo reported, that a cameraman’s camera was thrown to the ground, broken and then taken. [JPost reported](https://www.jpost.com/international/article-914884) the same account and, citing Le Monde, the crew’s composition. The ministry said at least one suspected attacker had been arrested. Meridian has not seen footage of the incident or a statement from BFMTV beyond the reporting above.

## Background

France 24 reported that protests also drew on opposition to a proposal to give police greater legal protection. France 24 described the day of action as protests over the rising cost of living and inequality.
